about: Relations of key links re-judged on 2026-11-12 (scripts/mapping/review_fixes.py applies them). Each was judged blind, statement against statement, against the LaTeX and the Lean at the pin; a verdict stronger than the earlier relation was not taken.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.cor_12_2_5.why: States only the second claim (12.42), and in weakened form: delta0>=2 instead of >=1, constant c+ replaced by 2 (book 1.36), cE truncated to 1.33258; first claim (over eq:jokor arcs) absent.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.etaU.why: Defines the weight η = η_2 *_M φ used in the corollary (∫ η_2(u/w) φ(w) dw/w).

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.cor_9_3_3.why: Same shape and main term, but requires x>=4 (book x>0) and uses a different error function err933N (its own for q>=2, an E2g/E1g-based form for q=1) instead of the explicit err of (eq:monte); equivalence/comparability of the error cannot be verified.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.etaU.why: Defines the weight eta_* = eta2 *_M phi (phi=t^2e^{-t^2/2}) used in the corollary; it exactly matches the corollary's definition of eta_* but is not the corollary's claim.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_S_eta2_le.how: review 2026-11-12, verified against the LaTeX and the Lean

TernaryGoldbach.circle_identity_tsum.why: States the outer equality for absolutely summable a,b,c (plus integrability), with sign convention e(n alpha), e(-N alpha); middle expression hat(f1*f2*f3) omitted.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.L.why: Exactly the L clause (no x argument, as the formula does not depend on x).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.Cxt.why: Only the inner log(1+...) of R, in terms of T=x^{1/3}; R = 0.27125 Cxt + 0.41415.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.majorArcs.why: Defines M_{delta0,r} (10.5); the intro's M here is a loosely defined (different) major-arc set, and the declaration is not the integral.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.integrand.why: The integrand S_{eta+}^2 S_{eta*} e(-N alpha), with x fixed to xOf N; the integration over M is not included.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.etaStar.why: Definition of a specific eta_* = (eta2 *_M phi)(49 t), an instance of the general eta_* in the item; not the identity.

TernaryGoldbach.expTsum.why: General exponential series sum a(n) e(n alpha); S_eta is the case a(n)=Lambda(n)eta(n/x).

TernaryGoldbach.Schar.why: General twisted sum sum a_n chi(n) e(n beta); item is a_n=Lambda(n)eta(n/x), beta=delta/x.

TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.SsumG.why: sum Lambda chi phi(n/x) for arbitrary complex phi; item is phi(t)=e(delta t)eta(t).

TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.fδ.why: Defines the function t^2 e^{-t^2/2} e(delta t) (a specific eta) whose Mellin transform is F_delta, not the transform itself.

TernaryGoldbach.expTsum.why: General exponential series; S_eta is the case a(n)=Lambda(n)eta(n/x).

TernaryGoldbach.e.why: Only the additive character e(t)=exp(2 pi i t) used in the definition.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.ramanujan_sum.why: Ramanujan sum written directly as sum over a<q coprime of e(an/q) (not as tau(chi_0,n)), and RHS indexed by d -> q/d with divisibility indicator; equivalent for q>=1.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.tri.why: Generic convolution \sum_{n_1+n_2+n_3=N} f(n_1)g(n_2)h(n_3) for real f,g,h; covers the display with f=\Lambda\cdot\eta_1(\cdot/x) only for real \eta_i and is not the specific sum.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.repSum.how: review 2026-11-12, verified against the LaTeX and the Lean

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.Cmain.why: Definition of the right-hand double integral (as (eta_o*eta_o) convolved with eta_*) for the specific eta_o, eta_*; not the identity.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.circle_identity.why: Evaluates this integral as the representation sum only for eta1=eta2=eta+, eta3=eta*, x=xOf N.

TernaryGoldbach.circle_identity_tsum.why: General identity: the integral over (0,1] of three absolutely summable exponential series times e(-N alpha) equals the triple convolution sum. It covers the surrounding claim (10.2)=(10.3) but is not the expression itself.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.gaussSum_one_e.why: States the core identity tau(chi_0)=mu(q) (chi_0 = conj chi_0 = trivial character) without the common factor hat eta3(-delta) x/phi(q).

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.fI.why: Only the integrand, for the specific weights eta1=eta2=eta+, eta3=eta*; no integral over M.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.integrand.why: Only the integrand, for the specific weights eta+, eta+, eta* and x=xOf N; no integral over M.

TernaryGoldbach.gaussSum_eq_sum_range.why: Only b=1: Mathlib gaussSum with stdAddChar equals sum_{c<N} chi(c) e(c/N).

TernaryGoldbach.stdAddChar_natCast_eq_e.why: Auxiliary fact stdAddChar(c)=e(c/N), not the Gauss sum.

TernaryGoldbach.Schar.why: General sum_n a_n chi(n) e(n beta); item is a_n=Lambda(n)eta(n/x).

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.Schar_eq_Ssum.why: Lemma identifying Schar with Ssum for the Gaussian weight; not the definition.

TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.SsumG.why: sum Lambda chi phi(n/x) for arbitrary complex phi, which includes phi(t)=e(beta x t)eta(t).

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.eta2.why: Defines eta2 by the explicit right-hand formula (0 for t<=0); the equality with eta1 *_M eta1 is not stated.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.theorem_3_1_1.why: Its second conjunct is exactly this bound, 0.276 x^{5/6}(log x)^{3/2} + 1234 x^{2/3} log x, under the same hypotheses; it also states the q <= x^{1/3}/6 case.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.P0.why: Only the [0,2] branch formula, without the restriction to [0,2] / zero elsewhere.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.conv2_ge.why: Lean proves only the lower bound conv2(rho) >= |eta_o|_2^2 - 8.82(2-rho)^2, for all rho, with a constant 8.82 that is weaker than 2.71|eta_o'|_2^2 (about 6.7-7.4); it is one-sided, its constant is weaker, and its range is wider, so neither statement implies the other.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.eta2.why: Defines the closed form 4 max(log 2 - |log 2t|,0) for t>0 (0 for t<=0); the identity with the Mellin convolution eta_1 *_M eta_1 is not stated.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.S.why: Lean's S fixes f(n) = Lambda(n) e(n alpha) (a tsum over n in N); the book's f is arbitrary.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.harmonic_le_G.why: The middle step H_n = sum_{r<=n} 1/r <= G(n), only for integers 1 <= n <= 199 (checked by computation).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.G_le_mul_Gq.why: Only the left inequality G(t) <= (P/phi(P)) G_P(t), and with the extra hypothesis that P is squarefree.

TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.f1pP.why: Only the local factor at a single p.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.f1p.why: Only the local factor at a single p.

TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.RamPf.cR.why: The definition gamma + sum_p log p/(p(p-1)) (sumP is a tsum over primes); the numerical value is not part of it.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.cE.why: The literal 1.33258, a rounded-down value used in place of c_E; it is not the constant itself.
The rounded constant 1.33258 that appears in the denominator.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.Sq.why: Only the subexpression S_q = sum_{p|q} log p/p; err_{q,R} itself is not defined.

TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.RamPf.ramare_boun.why: Exactly |G_d(R) - (phi(d)/d)(log R + c_E + S_d)| <= 7.284 R^{-1/3} f_1(d), for R > 0, which is wider than the book's R >= 1 (from (12.12)).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.kapQ.why: kappa(q), defined in the book at (12.31), with omega = 0.6274 and c_Delta = 0.0274177; an ingredient of lambda(q).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.Cxt.why: Same expression, but parametrised by T = z^{1/3} instead of z (Cxt (z^{1/3}) t = R^o_{z,t}).

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.thm_7_1_4_one.why: Bounds the same q=1 error for x >= 4.9e26, |delta| <= 6e5, but by 1e-18 + 6.24e6/sqrt(x); that is weaker than 1.1405e-8 near x_+ (about 2.8e-7) and stronger only for x above about 3e29, so neither statement implies the other.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.κ.why: Only the parameter choice kappa = 49 used in the display.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.xOf_denom_bound.why: Shows the denominator is positive and at most 2.02. This is a numerical fact about the definition, not the definition itself.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.xOf_ge.why: Only the first claim, xOf N >= 4.9e26 for N >= 10^27; x/kappa >= 1e25 is not stated.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.err_scaled_le_.why: A numerical lemma sqrt(c)(err(c) y + 1e-12 y) <= 1.49e-6 y; it plays the role of the sqrt(q*)|err| bound, but its constant is about 100x weaker than 1.33805e-8.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.prop_7_1_5'.why: States the first equality of the chain (error E2 with |E2| <= 2e-6 + 366.91/sqrt x) for x >= 4.9e26, which is the context range; the final O*(3e-6) inequality is not stated. It assumes Fact PlattGRH.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.prop_7_1_5.why: This is the same statement as prop_7_1_5' and is proved from it: only the first equality of the chain, for x >= 4.9e26.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.err_scaled_le.why: A purely numerical inequality, sqrt c * (err bound/sqrt c * x + 1e-15 x) <= 4.25e-7 x, used to combine the Lean constants. It does not bound err itself.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.integral_etaU.why: Gives the unscaled integral of eta_2 *_M phi as sqrt(pi/2), an ingredient (kappa = 1 version) rather than the statement about eta_*.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.integral_etaS.why: States the outer equality as the integral of eta_*(s) = etaU(kappa s), equal to sqrt(pi/2)/kappa. This is the integral rather than the L1 norm (equal because eta_* >= 0, but not stated), and the intermediate |eta_2|_1 |phi|_1 factorisation is absent.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.E_le_14_28.why: Bounds a different quantity: the sum over n not prime > sqrt x of (Lambda(n) eta_+(n/x))^2. The book's E is the explicit expression ((C_0+C_2) log x + ...) x^{1/2} of (eq:georgic) that bounds such a sum. The Lean constant 8e-11 is also weaker than 8.4029e-12.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.abs_etaPlus_le_.why: Gives |eta_+(t)| <= 1.94 for t >= 0, a weakened version of the sup-norm clause only (1.94 vs 1.079955).
Gives the crude bound |eta_+(t)| <= 400 for t >= 0, far weaker than the sup clause.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.sig.why: Defines the bounding function used in T_le.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.sig_le_lin.why: sig(x) ≤ 0.640208000017 log x − 0.021095 for x ≥ 4.9e26; combined with T_le it gives S ≤ 0.640208000017 x log x − 0.021095 x.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.circle_identity.why: Gives the identity (plus integrability) over (0,1] with weights eta(n_i/x), correcting the book's missing /x. It fixes x = xOf N where the book's identity holds for any x, and requires N > 0.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.integrand.why: Definition of the right-hand integrand S_{eta_+}^2 S_{eta_*} e(-N alpha) at x = xOf N, not the identity.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.repSum.why: Definition of the left-hand weighted representation sum (with a predicate filter) at x = xOf N, not the identity.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.nonprime_input.why: A downstream numerical consequence: repSum(all) - repSum(odd primes) <= 6.7e6 N sqrt N log N for N >= 10^27, obtained after inserting crude sup bounds and Chebyshev estimates.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.repSum_sub_le_o.why: States the outer inequality of the chain: repSum(all) - repSum(Good) <= 3 Ap^2 As log N (psi(N) - theta(N) + log 2) psi(N), with Ap and As any bounds on |eta_+| and |eta_*| on t >= 0 in place of the sup norms. The middle step is absent, and the weights carry /x = xOf N.

TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.prod_lower_bou.why: Bounds a finite product over odd primes 3 <= p <= R, for R >= 200, below by 0.6606(1 - 1/199). This is a different quantity (the truncated product, which exceeds the infinite one), and twice the bound is 1.3146 < 1.3203.

MellinConvergent.why: The integrability predicate for the Mellin integral, i.e. the l_1 condition discussed after the display, not the transform itself.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.mellinConv.why: The same formula, int_{r>0} f(r) g(t/r)/r, but only for real-valued f and g (the book's functions are general).

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.S.why: Same sum (as a tsum over n, alpha real rather than in R/Z), but Lean only allows a real-valued weight eta : R -> R, while the book allows complex-valued eta.

TernaryGoldbach.e.why: e(t) = exp(2 pi i t) is defined in the surrounding text and used in the display; it is not the display's definition of S_eta.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeII.why: typeII is the Type II sum S_II with f = 1_odd (v = 2) built in; it uses this f but does not define it.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.L.why: Exactly the L_{x,t,q} clause; the formula does not depend on x, so Lean drops x as an argument.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.Cxt.why: C_{x,t} = log(1 + ...) (written with T = x^{1/3}) is only the inner logarithm of R_{x,t} (R = 0.27125 C + 0.41415); it is not one of the display's clauses.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.trunc.why: Defines the truncation f_{<=U}, which the display uses, not the identity.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.vaughan.how: review 2026-11-12, verified against the LaTeX and the Lean

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeI2.why: The S_{I,2} clause (sums over v <= V, u <= U, n), specialised to f = 1_odd (v = 2) and eta = eta_2.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeILog.why: The S_{I,1} clause with U = D, specialised to f = 1_odd and eta = eta_2.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.S0inf.why: The S_{0,infty} clause, specialised to f = 1_odd and eta = eta_2.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeII.why: The S_II clause, specialised to f = 1_odd and eta = eta_2. m runs over all odd m <= x, but terms with m <= U vanish because the inner divisor sum over d > U is then empty.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.sum_inv_le.why: Only the first inequality of the chain (divided by x): sum_{j<J} 1/(R+jq) <= 1/R + (1/q) log(D/R), for any R, q > 0 and any J with R + (J-1)q <= D. The second inequality is not stated.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeI.why: The same sum with eta fixed to eta_2, which the lemma leaves general. The finite range n <= x is harmless because supp eta_2 is in [1/4, 1].

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.Mof.why: A specific choice M = min(x/(2|delta|q), D) (D if delta = 0) of the parameter M, which the book only requires to lie in [min(Q0/2, D), D].

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_restPart_.why: Proves that the non-main terms are at most bound_4_31, under case-(b)-type hypotheses. It is a claim using the expression, not the expression itself.
Proves that the non-main terms (with M = Mof) are at most bound_4_32 for |delta| >= 1/2c2. It is a claim using the expression, not the expression itself.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.Todd.why: The same sum with the weight fixed to eta_2.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.SmoothData.nor.why: The same three bounds for any continuous, compactly supported g with |g|_1 <= N, total variation <= V and (2pi t)^2|g^(t)| <= K (giving x N/2m + V/2, V/2/|sin|, (m/x)(K/2)/sin^2). With N = 1 this is the book's case, and Lean drops piecewise C^2. The last two bounds are stated for sin != 0, where the book's min is otherwise trivial.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_Todd_le.why: The same three bounds, but only for eta = eta_2, with |eta'|_1 = 8 log 2 and c0 fixed to 32.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.c₂_identity.why: The same identity (with c2 = 6pi/5sqrt(c0)), but proved only for the fixed value c0 = 32; in the book it holds for any c0 > 0.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.c₂.why: The definition c2 = 6pi/(5 sqrt c0) from the preceding text, which the identity follows from; it is not the identity.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeILog.why: The same sum with eta fixed to eta_2.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_restPartL.why: Proves that the non-main terms of the log-weighted Type I sum are at most bound_4_41. It is a claim using the expression, not the expression itself.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.sum_R1L.why: The same bound for eta = eta_2 and c0 = 32, but the sum runs over m <= min(q/2, D) with the extra hypothesis D <= x/4. This is a sub-sum of non-negative terms, so the claim is weaker.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeI2.why: The same triple sum with eta fixed to eta_2. The absolute value is taken at the use site, not in the definition.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.lemma_4_1_2.why: Same hypotheses and bound, but Lean's C/0 = 0 makes the summand 0 instead of A where sin(pi alpha n) = 0 (possible when q not| n only in degenerate cases). The left side can only shrink, so the claim is at most slightly weaker.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_mainPartI.why: Proves that the terms with q | a <= M are at most bound_4_50 (the corrected expression). It also assumes the PlattGRH input. It is a claim using the expression, not the expression itself.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.c₄.why: The constant c4 = 1.03884 used in the display. It is defined later in the proof, not by this display.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_restPartI.why: Proves ||restPartI2|| <= sum_{n<=UV, not(q|n and n<=M)} log n |T_{n,o}|, the reduction to (an absolute-value form of) this sum with eta_2 and the oddness of m dropped. It is a step that uses the expression.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.restPartI2.why: The same range of m (odd, not(q|m and m<=M)), but with coefficient c(a) = sum Lambda(v) mu(a/v) instead of log m: it is the quantity before applying |c(a)| <= log a.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.lemma_4_1_3.why: Same hypotheses (Approx = alpha = a/q + beta/qQ, (a,q)=1, |beta|<=1, q<=Q; y2-y1<=q, y2<=Q/2, B,C>=0) and the same bound. Lean also proves the second bound of the lemma, (2Bq/pi) log(2e^2 q/pi), in the same statement.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.typeII.how: review 2026-11-12, verified against the LaTeX and the Lean

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.lemma_5_1_1.why: Lean states Lemma 5.1.1 for v=2 (main term 4z/pi^2 = 6z/pi^2 * v/sigma(v)) with exactly this error bound. The l-range lower end is max(z/(y r1), z/(y r2), z/(2r1r2)), where the book's (5.9) prints min, a typo given (5.8). r <= floor y vs r < y changes nothing.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.integral_g2.why: Proves the identity behind the rewriting for one s (y = S/s, v=2): int_{1/2}^1 g2(uy) du = sum mu mu/(sigma sigma) (1 - max(1/2, r1/y, r2/y)). The weighted sum over s and the prefactor are not stated.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.g2_eq_sum_dvd.why: The v=2 case of the equality of g with the second line: sum_d mu(d) (sum_{d|r} f(r))^2, with f = mu/sigma on odd r.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.g2_eq_sum_moeb.why: The v=2 case of the equality of g with the last line: sum_{d<=N} mu(d) f(d)^2 S_d(N/d)^2, where f(d)^2 = 1/sigma(d)^2 for odd squarefree d, the oddness of f gives (d,2)=1, and S_d sums over odd r coprime to d. The intermediate equalities are not stated, and the v=1 case is not covered.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.IIsum.why: Defines only the integrand of the right side (v=2). The m-range starts at x/2W, which is harmless because c_m = 0 for m <= U. It states no claim.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.T2_le'.why: Only the v=2 case, T2(S) <= 0.37273. It holds for S >= 16, wider than the displayed S >= 100000 (the book's text extends it to 16 <= S). It assumes Ramare's Moebius bound as a Fact.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.T2_le.why: A restatement of T2_le': the v=2 case for S >= 16.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.S1_bound.why: Proves only the upper half of the O* statement (S1 <= ...), for x, W > 0 and U >= 1. Lean's H2 uses max(T2,0) where the book uses G2, so Lean's H2 is at most the book's.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.H2.why: Defines only H2, and for S<16 uses (4/pi^2) max(T2(S),0) in place of the book's computable upper bound (4/pi^2) G2(S). H1 is absent.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.H2_le.why: Only the H2 <= 2/pi^2 clause, for all S, with Lean's H2 (max(T2,0) in place of G2).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.primeExpSum.why: Defines only the inner prime sum S(beta) = sum_{W'<p<=W} log p e(beta p).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.oddSqSum.why: The same sum over odd m with a free upper endpoint A1 in place of x/W, which is only a reparametrisation. v=2 is fixed.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.S2.why: Exactly the definition with v=2 fixed (m odd).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.primeExpSum.why: Defines only the inner prime sum, with general endpoints.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.S1.why: The S1 clause, with v=2 (odd m).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.S2.why: The S2 clause, with v=2, and general U', W' standing for max(U,x/2W) and max(V,W/2).

TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.sum_inv_le_sum_in.why: The second inequality, sum_{n<=N} 1/n <= sum_{r<=N squarefree} 1/phi(r), for natural N.

TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.log_le_sum_coprim.why: The outer inequality of the chain, with R left free (R >= 0): (phi(q)/q) log R <= sum. Setting R = (q(nu+upsilon))^{-1/2} gives the printed right end. The intermediate links are not stated.

TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.sum_sqfree_div_to.why: The first inequality, generalised to a non-negative antitone weight w (w=1 gives the book's step).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.lemma_5_2_3_a.how: review 2026-11-12, verified against the LaTeX and the Lean

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.prop_5_2_4_a.why: Same bound. Lean drops Prop 5.2.4's x >= W >= 1 and Q >= 3.5W (it needs only x, W > 0). Its extra assumptions rho > 0 and W' <= W cost nothing: rho = 0 is vacuous, and W' > W makes both sides 0.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.prop_5_2_4_b.why: Same bound. Lean needs only q <= Q, x, W > 0, W' >= W/2 and U' >= x/2W, dropping the proposition's Q >= 3.5W and x >= W >= 1.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.prop_5_2_4_d.why: Same bound and the same delta and rho conditions. Lean drops the proposition's Q >= 3.5W and x >= W >= 1.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.S1.why: Exactly the definition with v=2 fixed (m odd). v is a free parameter in the book here.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.innerS.why: Defines only the inner sum for fixed s (y = B/Us, z = B/s, B = x/W), with v=2. It states no equality.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.eVariationOn_et.why: The second clause, stated as total variation of eta2 = 8 log 2.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.eta2_L1.why: The first clause, |eta2|_1 = 1 (an alias of integral_abs_eta2).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.eta2'L1.why: Only defines the constant 8 log 2 under the name |eta2'|_1. It states no claim about eta2.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.logSqSum.why: Defines the left-hand sum over primes in (floor W', floor W].

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.logSqSum_le_ha.how: review 2026-11-12, verified against the LaTeX and the Lean

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.integral_abs_e.why: The first clause, non-strict (<= log rho).

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.eVariationOn_e.why: The second clause as a non-strict upper bound: total variation <= 8 log 2 log rho. The exact value 2 log(rho/2) eta2(1/2) is not stated.

TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.integral_inv_m.how: review 2026-11-12, verified against the LaTeX and the Lean

Bounds Lean's lower-order-term expression by 3.2 x^{5/6}. That is a different expression from the book's terms.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.sH.why: F_H(e^v) = (H/pi) sinc(Hv), a reparametrisation in v = log y with the singularity removed. Not the printed definition.

TernaryGoldbach.Helfgott.hH.why: The second line (h_H as a Mellin convolution), with H free.

TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.Gr.why: A rotated-contour integral that equals G_delta at theta = 0. A different quantity.
